reason: Phase 5 carries three reusable rules: an asynchronous lifecycle needs a generation owner (open before the first await, check after each one, invalidation must not be sticky), a shell-like grammar on a surface that executes its arguments is a security interface (one flag per verbatim argument, and a refusal that teaches the new form), and a boundary that carries no output forces every caller to re-implement collection. Plus the recurring kata-CLI evidence-schema collision and the mechanical validation to run after every seal.
